image_description: Three Nile crocodiles resting on a sandy bank. The top crocodile has its mouth wide open, displaying teeth and the interior of the mouth. The bottom-left crocodile also has its mouth open but less widely. The bottom-right crocodile has its mouth closed. All exhibit textured, armored skin with visible osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All three heads clearly show the characteristic V-shaped snout and broad triangular shape typical of crocodiles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two of the three crocodiles have their mouths open, so teeth visibility 'when mouth is closed' cannot be fully verified for them. The bottom-right crocodile has a closed mouth, but the angle makes it difficult to confirm the specific interlocking pattern (4th lower tooth in notch) definitively. However, visible teeth appear conical and numerous.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Eyes are clearly dorsal. Vertical slit pupils are visible on the bottom-left crocodile. Nictitating membrane is not clearly visible due to resolution/angle, but eye structure is consistent.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Nostrils are clearly visible at the distal end of the snouts on all subjects.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Bodies are elongated and covered in heavy armor/scutes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal surfaces show clear, regular longitudinal rows of raised, bony scutes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Coloration is greyish-brown with high texture detail consistent with osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The crocodiles are viewed from a dorsal/lateral angle; the ventral surface (belly) is occluded by the ground or body position.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are largely occluded by the bodies of the crocodiles or the sand. Digits and webbing details are not clearly visible to verify count.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail of the top crocodile is visible, showing lateral compression and muscular structure. Proportion seems consistent with species norms.

artifact_observations.location: Interior of the mouth of the top crocodile
artifact_observations.reasoning: The pink tissue inside the mouth appears slightly overly smooth and plastic-like compared to the highly detailed exterior scales, lacking fine mucosal texture.

artifact_observations.location: Jaw hinge area of the bottom-left crocodile
artifact_observations.reasoning: The connection between the lower jaw and the skull appears slightly ambiguous and soft, lacking a clear mechanical hinge definition, suggesting minor structural melting.

artifact_observations.location: Teeth edges of the top crocodile
artifact_observations.reasoning: Some teeth tips show slight softness/bleeding into the background air, typical of AI generation sharpness issues.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification (Nile Crocodile vs other crocodilians) based on snout shape and scale patterns.
To check for fusion artifacts between teeth and gums, and ensure the open mouths have valid topological boundaries without melting.
To analyze the realism of the complex scale textures and identify any repetitive patterns or smearing indicative of AI generation.
To verify the spatial relationship between the three crocodiles and ensure no impossible overlapping or depth bleeding occurs.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the interior of the open mouths. AI often struggles with the transition from hard scales to soft tissue. Check if the teeth are individually distinct or if they merge into the gum line. Verify if the 'closed mouth' crocodile actually shows the characteristic 4th tooth interlock if visible.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
